summary:
The Sai-Moon help users to explore and compare potential lunar landing sites through an interactive lunar map. Users can select locations, review key conditions such as terrain, sunlight, and communication visibility, and compare candidates against mission needs. By bringing these considerations together in one clear experience, the Navigator makes it easier to identify promising sites and understand the trade-offs involved in planning a lunar landing.
The platform organizes this information around mission requirements, making candidate sites easier to compare. This matters because it turns lunar and astronomical data into a clearer basis for evaluating locations and planning future surface missions.
details:
Sai-Moon is an interactive experience for exploring the Moon. It presents a visual lunar environment and lets users interact with the features available on screen to learn more about the Moon’s surface and our natural satellite.

The project aims to make lunar exploration more accessible and engaging. By combining visualization and interaction, it can spark curiosity about the Moon and help students and the general public become more familiar with space exploration. Our intended impact is to encourage learning and interest in science and future lunar missions.

We developed Sai-Moon as a web application using TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, and deployed it on Vercel. We designed the experience to be visual, easy to navigate, and suitable for a short presentation.

Sai-Moon’s creative approach is to turn lunar exploration into an interactive experience rather than presenting information only as static text. During development, we considered interface clarity, ease of use, visual appeal, and how to make the available features engaging.
